title: Arjuna breaks down and Krishna begins to teach

verses.sa: सञ्जय उवाचतं तथा कृपयाऽविष्टमश्रुपूर्णाकुलेक्षणम् । विषीदन्तमिदं वाक्यमुवाच मधुसूदनः ॥
verses.tr: Sanjaya says: To Arjuna, overcome by pity, his eyes full of tears and clouded with grief, Madhusudana spoke these words.
verses.speaker: Sanjaya

intro.text: Sanjaya paints a picture of Arjuna sitting broken on his chariot, and then Krishna begins to speak to him.

body.text: Sanjaya says: To Arjuna, overcome by pity, his eyes full of tears and clouded with grief, Madhusudana spoke these words. Madhusudana, the slayer of the demon Madhu, is the name Krishna takes as he begins this teaching to a weeping Arjuna. Krishna asks Arjuna where this delusion has come from in this moment of crisis.

verses.sa: श्री भगवानुवाचकुतस्त्वा कश्मलमिदं विषमे समुपस्थितम् । अनार्यजुष्टमस्वर्ग्यमकीर्तिकरमर्जुन ॥
verses.tr: Krishna says: Arjuna, where has this delusion come from in this crisis? Noble people do not follow it. It does not lead upward, and it brings disgrace.
verses.angle: kashmalam: the delusion unfollowed by the noble
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna's first words are a direct rebuke. Listen for the one word he uses to name Arjuna's sudden collapse.

body.text: Krishna says: Arjuna, where has this delusion come from in this crisis? Noble people do not follow it. It does not lead upward, and it brings disgrace. Krishna names the collapse as kashmalam, delusion. He says it has no place here because noble people do not follow it, it leads nowhere higher, and it brings disgrace. He tells Arjuna to cast off this petty weakness of heart and rise to fight.

verses.sa: क्लैब्यं मा स्म गमः पार्थ नैतत्त्वय्युपपद्यते । क्षुद्रं हृदयदौर्बल्यं त्यक्त्वोत्तिष्ठ परन्तप ॥
verses.tr: Do not yield to weakness, Partha. It does not suit you. Cast off this petty weakness of heart and rise, scorcher of foes.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Arjuna has collapsed into grief and doubt. Krishna cuts through it with a sharp question and a direct command. Listen for how he names the moment.

body.text: Do not yield to weakness, Partha. It does not suit you. Cast off this petty weakness of heart and rise, scorcher of foes. Krishna calls Arjuna by two names, Partha, son of Pritha, and Parantapa, scorcher of foes. He tells him to cast off the petty weakness of heart, because it does not suit who he is. Arjuna replies that he cannot raise his bow against Bhishma and Drona, who are worthy of his worship.

verses.sa: अर्जुन उवाचकथं भीष्ममहं संख्ये द्रोणं च मधुसूदन । इषुभिः प्रतियोत्स्यामि पूजार्हावरिसूदन ॥
verses.tr: Arjuna says: How can I fight Bhishma and Drona with arrows in battle, O Madhusudana? They are worthy of worship, O destroyer of enemies.
verses.angle: Arjuna's dilemma over fighting his teachers
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: After Krishna rebukes Arjuna for his despair, Arjuna answers with a deeper wound: how can he shoot arrows at the teachers he reveres?

body.text: Arjuna says: How can I fight Bhishma and Drona with arrows in battle, O Madhusudana? They are worthy of worship, O destroyer of enemies. Arjuna asks how he can fight Bhishma and Drona with arrows, and calls them worthy of worship, revealing the depth of his anguish. Sanjaya answers with the king's own son, Duryodhana, looking across at the Pandava army.

verses.sa: गुरूनहत्वा हि महानुभावान्श्रेयो भोक्तुं भैक्ष्यमपीह लोके । हत्वार्थकामांस्तु गुरूनिहैवभुञ्जीय भोगान् रुधिरप्रदिग्धान् ॥
verses.tr: It is better to live on alms in this world than to kill these great teachers. If I kill them, the pleasures I enjoy here will be stained with blood and bound to greed.
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Krishna has asked Arjuna to act, but Arjuna now answers with a moral cost. He names the people standing against him as his own teachers.

body.text: It is better to live on alms in this world than to kill these great teachers. If I kill them, the pleasures I enjoy here will be stained with blood and bound to greed. Listen to how he weighs his duty against his respect. He says that winning these pleasures stained with blood is worse than living on alms, and that any victory he takes is bound to greed. Next, Arjuna continues.

verses.sa: न चैतद्विद्मः कतरन्नो गरीयोयद्वा जयेम यदि वा नो जयेयुः । यानेव हत्वा न जिजीविषामस्तेऽवस्थिताः प्रमुखे धार्तराष्ट्राः ॥
verses.tr: We do not know which is better for us: to fight or not to fight. We do not even know whether we will conquer them or they us. The sons of Dhritarashtra stand before us, and we do not wish to live after killing them.
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna stands between two armies with his bow lowered. He admits he cannot tell which is better, or who will win.

body.text: We do not know which is better for us: to fight or not to fight. We do not even know whether we will conquer them or they us. The sons of Dhritarashtra stand before us, and we do not wish to live after killing them. Arjuna admits he cannot tell whether fighting or not fighting is better, or which side would win. He now asks Krishna to tell him with certainty what is best, because he is confused about his duty.

verses.sa: कार्पण्यदोषोपहतस्वभावःपृच्छामि त्वां धर्मसंमूढचेताः । यच्छ्रेयः स्यान्निश्िचतं ब्रूहि तन्मेशिष्यस्तेऽहं शाधि मां त्वां प्रपन्नम् ॥
verses.tr: My nature is overwhelmed by weakness, and my mind is confused about duty. I ask you: tell me with certainty what is best for me. I am your student; instruct me, for I have taken refuge in you.
verses.angle: Disciple and refuge: the teaching begins
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna has dropped his bow. Listen for how he stops arguing and calls Krishna his teacher.

body.text: My nature is overwhelmed by weakness, and my mind is confused about duty. I ask you: tell me with certainty what is best for me. I am your student; instruct me, for I have taken refuge in you. He calls himself your student, your disciple, and one who has taken refuge. With that single shift, the debate ends and the teaching begins. He then lists all the kingdoms and wealth he could win, and finds they cannot touch his grief.

verses.sa: न हि प्रपश्यामि ममापनुद्याद्यच्छोकमुच्छोषणमिन्द्रियाणाम् । अवाप्य भूमावसपत्नमृद्धम्राज्यं सुराणामपि चाधिपत्यम् ॥
verses.tr: Even if I gained an unrivaled, prosperous kingdom on earth or lordship over the gods, I see nothing that could remove this grief that dries up my senses.
verses.angle: Arjuna rejects both earthly and divine rewards
verses.speaker: Arjuna

intro.text: Arjuna has just confessed his weakness and confusion. Now he tells Krishna that no power on earth or in heaven can dry up his grief.

body.text: Even if I gained an unrivaled, prosperous kingdom on earth or lordship over the gods, I see nothing that could remove this grief that dries up my senses. Listen to the scale of what Arjuna rejects. He is not talking about a small kingdom, but an unrivaled, prosperous earth and even lordship over the gods. Sanjaya then reports that after hearing this, Arjuna firmly tells Krishna he will not fight and falls silent.

verses.sa: सञ्जय उवाचएवमुक्त्वा हृषीकेशं गुडाकेशः परन्तप । न योत्स्य इति गोविन्दमुक्त्वा तूष्णीं बभूव ह ॥
verses.tr: Sanjaya says: Having spoken thus to Hrishikesha, Gudakesha, the scorcher of foes, said to Govinda, “I will not fight,” and fell silent.
verses.angle: Gudakesha, the conqueror of sleep, falls silent
verses.speaker: Sanjaya

intro.text: Arjuna has refused to fight, and now the battlefield falls silent. Listen to how Sanjaya describes that sudden stillness.

body.text: Sanjaya says: Having spoken thus to Hrishikesha, Gudakesha, the scorcher of foes, said to Govinda, “I will not fight,” and fell silent. Sanjaya calls Arjuna Gudakesha, the conqueror of sleep, and then says he fell silent. The man who controlled sleep now surrenders to grief, and the battlefield holds its breath. Krishna then steps forward to speak to the silent Arjuna, and the crisis begins to shift.

verses.sa: तमुवाच हृषीकेशः प्रहसन्निव भारत । सेनयोरुभयोर्मध्ये विषीदन्तमिदं वचः ॥
verses.tr: Hrsikesa spoke to the grieving Arjuna, smiling slightly, in the midst of the two armies.
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Arjuna has just dropped his bow, saying he will not fight. What does Krishna say to him, standing right there between the two armies?

body.text: Hrsikesa spoke to the grieving Arjuna, smiling slightly, in the midst of the two armies. Krishna speaks as if smiling at Arjuna's grief. The name Hrishikesha means lord of the senses, and here he stands between two armies to teach the master of the senses how to act. Krishna gently points out that Arjuna is grieving for the wrong reasons while speaking like a wise man.

verses.sa: श्री भगवानुवाचअशोच्यानन्वशोचस्त्वं प्रज्ञावादांश्च भाषसे । गतासूनगतासूंश्च नानुशोचन्ति पण्डिताः ॥
verses.tr: The Blessed Lord says: You grieve for what should not be grieved for, yet speak words of wisdom. The wise do not grieve for the dead or the living.
verses.angle: Wisdom and grief do not match in Arjuna
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna looks at Arjuna's words and actions, finding a mismatch. Listen for the gap between what Arjuna says and what he does.

body.text: The Blessed Lord says: You grieve for what should not be grieved for, yet speak words of wisdom. The wise do not grieve for the dead or the living. Krishna points out the mismatch: Arjuna speaks like a wise man while grieving for those who need no grief. Krishna then reminds Arjuna that neither he nor the kings will ever cease to exist.

verses.sa: न त्वेवाहं जातु नासं न त्वं नेमे जनाधिपाः । न चैव न भविष्यामः सर्वे वयमतः परम् ॥
verses.tr: I was never absent, nor were you, nor these kings. Nor will any of us cease to be in the future.
verses.angle: jaatu: at any time, showing no beginning or end
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna is correcting Arjuna's grief by pointing to a word that keeps coming back. Listen for it.

body.text: I was never absent, nor were you, nor these kings. Nor will any of us cease to be in the future. The word jaatu, meaning at any time, appears in the verse. By saying there was never a time when any of us were not, Krishna shows that existence has no beginning and no end. Krishna then explains how the embodied soul simply moves from one body to another like changing clothes.

verses.sa: देहिनोऽस्मिन्यथा देहे कौमारं यौवनं जरा । तथा देहान्तरप्राप्तिर्धीरस्तत्र न मुह्यति ॥
verses.tr: Just as the embodied one passes through childhood, youth, and old age in this body, so too it passes into another body. The wise are not deluded by this.
verses.angle: Dehinah: the embodied one that moves
verses.speaker: Krishna

intro.text: Krishna is speaking to Arjuna, who is terrified at the thought of killing his own kin. Listen to how Krishna uses a simple human experience to steady him.

body.text: Just as the embodied one passes through childhood, youth, and old age in this body, so too it passes into another body. The wise are not deluded by this. The word dehinah, the embodied one, is the subject here. It is the one who moves from childhood to old age and then into another body, and the steady one is not deluded by this. Krishna now brings in the senses and the heat and cold that come with them.
